policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly renders the qere sense with 'his eyes were enlightened,' distinguishing וַתָּאֹרְנָה from the ketiv ותראנה ('saw').
ASV 'the people flew upon the spoil' directly renders the qere וַיַּעַט ('flew/rushed upon'), rather than the ketiv ויעש ('did/made').
ASV 'upon the spoil' includes the definite article, matching the qere הַשָּׁלָל and distinguishing it from the anarthrous ketiv שלל.
